messages.content: Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.
Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating‑point numbers have a finite precision, so each operation rounds the exact real result to the nearest representable value. When you add three numbers as \((a+b)+c\) versus \(a+(b+c)\), the intermediate rounding can differ, causing the two final rounded results to be unequal. Hence the rounding errors introduced at each step break the mathematical associativity of addition.
